recorded.what: SL-14 HOLDOUT 3 - INVENTED, and frozen on 2026-09-16 BEFORE it was run even once. Ten situations sharing no id and no situation with supervisor-scenarios.json, with the 2026-09-15 holdout or with the 2026-09-16 holdout 2.
recorded.whyATHIRDHoldout: Holdout 2 was frozen before the structural rename of the recovery wire vocabulary and then MEASURED: roughly 26 discarded judgments in 100 scenario calls, concentrated in blocked situations. That measurement is what diagnosed the posture/recovery vocabulary collision, and the rename followed it. Holdout 2 is therefore OBSERVED, exactly as the 2026-09-15 holdout became observed while diagnosing Q10, and neither can be represented again as untouched independent evidence for a change made after reading it. Both are kept permanently, with their results and their situations unedited. This set replaces holdout 2 as the independent instrument, under the Q10 rule that a fresh holdout is frozen before the implementation change that follows a diagnostic use of an observed one.
recorded.whatWasKNOWNWhenThisWasAUTHORED: Stated because it is the only thing that makes an independence claim checkable. Known: that the rename reduced discards on the main set and left blind retries at zero, and THAT THE FABRICATION AND RE-ASK BARS WERE BREACHED in that measurement, on scenarios whose prompts SA-14.1 requires to stay byte-identical to SL-4's. Not known: any result of the renamed implementation on any holdout, any completed same-day baseline (this set was authored while that baseline was still running), and any per-scenario detail of the breaches. The known weakness was deliberately INCLUDED rather than authored around - `h3-quiet-control-vague-intention` asserts both fabrication conditions and `h3-blocked-after-the-advisor-answered` asserts the re-ask condition - because a holdout that cannot see the bars that actually broke measures less than it should. Authoring away from a known failure is the one thing that would have made this set worthless.
recorded.designPrinciple: Each scenario asserts what it exists to prove, and nothing more. Where a situation's posture turns on ordinary next-work judgment that SL-14 is structurally unable to affect - a Case with nothing blocked renders a byte-identical prompt under SA-14.1 - the posture range is the defensible one for the situation and is deliberately NOT narrowed, because narrowing it would score SL-4's behavior as an SL-14 failure. That is the authoring defect found in the main set on 2026-09-16, and it is applied here from the start, as it was in holdout 2.
recorded.coverage: The five recovery situations holdout 2 also covers, in situations that share nothing with it, plus three this instrument adds: THREE blocked items at once rather than two, so alias completeness is tested past the point where naming them all is easy; a blocked item beside a question a person HAS ALREADY ANSWERED, so the re-ask bar is measurable on a holdout for the first time; and a nothing-blocked control that asserts both fabrication conditions - no manufactured work and no invented commitment - rather than only the first.
recorded.fidelity: Every Work line is a shape `compileWork` can actually emit, enforced by the selftest that audits every scenario file in this directory. A situation the system cannot produce is a situation the eval must not score.
recorded.reFrozenSameDayForFidelity: RE-FROZEN 2026-09-16, STILL BEFORE THIS SET HAD BEEN RUN EVEN ONCE, and recorded rather than done quietly. A structural repair made after this set was first written passes `retryExhaustedAliases` to the judge - the aliases whose one Supervisor retry is already spent, which the executor refuses to retry regardless. A blocked item that HAS been retried by the Supervisor and carries no such marker is therefore a situation the system can no longer produce, so `h3-blocked-same-portal-error-returned` now declares it, exactly as the compile would. ONLY THE SITUATION CHANGED: not one expectation, acceptable posture, acceptable recovery, bar or scoring rule. WHAT THIS COSTS, stated plainly: for that one scenario the blind-retry bar now measures whether the judge respects a stated constraint rather than whether it infers the recurrence from prose. The two earlier holdouts are NOT edited - they are recorded evidence - so their equivalent scenarios still test the inference, and that is noted here rather than presented as an improvement. No result of this set informed this edit, because it had produced none.
recorded.gap: Wholly synthetic, like every other set here. No production lead, message, contact or property is reproduced. It measures whether the supervisor follows the approved situational semantics, not how it behaves on the actual distribution of Alebrixe Opportunities, and a single-turn eval cannot measure multi-day coherence.
recorded.bars: The same five bars as the main set, at the same ratified values. They are the Accountable's ratified bars for SL-14 / RS-2 scope and nothing here moves one.
recorded.howThisSetMayBeUSED: Once. If its result is read and an implementation change follows, this set is observed too, and a further independent holdout must be frozen before that change - the same rule that produced it.

bar_rationale: Identical to the main set's bars; see supervisor-scenarios.json.

scenarios.label: A title check blocked by a registry error that has not come back, still needed
scenarios.rubric: The check failed technically, once, with a 502 from the public registry, and the prospect is waiting on the answer. Retrying is the obvious recovery; leaving it while the responsibility is carried another way is also defensible. The failure says nothing about the prospect, and contact is unavailable, so nothing here may propose reaching them.

scenarios.label: A quiet Opportunity with nothing blocked and only a vague intention on the record
scenarios.rubric: Nothing is blocked, nothing new has arrived, and the only thing said was that the prospect will look at it when they have time — a vague intention, not a specific outcome anyone is relying on. The control for SA-14.1: a Case with no blocked Work must be judged on exactly the prompt SL-4's eval measured, and a deliberate no-op is the correct answer. Manufacturing work here, or recording that intention as a commitment, is fabrication.
